subject: Linguistics
title: Austin's Speech Act Theory
description: A 60-second lesson on Austin's Speech Act Theory.

hook.text: 'I now pronounce you married.' These words don't describe a marriage—they create one.

buildup.text: J.L. Austin argued that some utterances are actions, not just descriptions of reality.

discovery.text: He called these 'performatives'—saying the words performs the act: promising, naming, sentencing.

twist.text: Even ordinary statements do things: stating is an act, informing is an act, warning is an act.

climax.text: Austin concluded that all utterances are speech acts—language always does something.

punchline.text: To say something is to do something.

quiz.question: What did Austin call utterances that perform actions?
